samasa.literal: of the host of the fathers
samasa.sense: of the ancestors, to whom śrāddha offerings are made

morph.note: सुरता is सुर ‘god’ with the taddhita -ता in the collective sense (‘a body of gods’), formed like जनता ‘a body of people’.
Passive of the causative: उत् + चारि (√चर् + ṇic) + yak + से; the causative’s -i- is lost before the passive -य-. ‘You are made to sound, are pronounced’.

स्वाहा and स्वधा are indeclinable ritual words, the calls that accompany offerings to the gods and to the ancestors. The hymn treats them as names of the Goddess and makes them predicates (‘you are Svāhā’).

mantras.anvaya: देवि, सकलेषु मखेषु यस्याः समुदीरणेन समस्तसुरता तृप्तिं प्रयाति, (सा त्वं) स्वाहा असि वै। पितृगणस्य च तृप्तिहेतुः (त्वम्), अतः एव त्वं जनैः स्वधा च उच्चार्यसे।
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause (यस्याः … प्रयाति) and its main clause (स्वाहा असि वै), then a second sentence with a passive verb whose agent is जनैः and whose predicate nominative is स्वधा.
mantras.lit: O Devī, you by whose utterance in all sacrifices the whole company of the gods attains satisfaction — you are indeed Svāhā; and, being the cause of the satisfaction of the host of ancestors, for that very reason you are pronounced by people as Svadhā too.
mantras.tr: O Devī, at every sacrifice it is by the uttering of you that all the gods together are satisfied: you are Svāhā. And because you satisfy the host of the ancestors, people utter you as Svadhā.

comm.t: Svāhā is spoken as an oblation is poured into the fire for the gods; Svadhā when it is offered to the ancestors. The hymn identifies the Goddess with these sacred words themselves: the gods and the ancestors are fed through her.

Brahmā’s hymn in chapter 1 already said त्वं स्वाहा त्वं स्वधा (1.73). Here the identification is explained: she is Svāhā because the gods are satisfied by her utterance, Svadhā because the ancestors are.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has the same pair of names side by side: स्वाहा (name 535) and स्वधा (name 536).

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi containing karmadhārayas (अविचिन्त्यमहाव्रत; महाव्रत = महत् व्रतम्)
samasa.literal: she whose great vow is unthinkable
samasa.sense: she whose great observance is beyond thought
samasa.alt: The feminine ending (व्रत is neuter) shows a bahuvrīhi. Whether the ‘great vow’ is the Goddess’s own or the discipline by which the sages reach her is left open by the compound; the next words (अभ्यस्यसे … मुनिभिः) favour the second.

samasa.vigraha: सुनियतानि इन्द्रियाणि येषां ते सुनियतेन्द्रियाः; तत्त्वं सारः येषां ते तत्त्वसाराः; सुनियतेन्द्रियाः च ते तत्त्वसाराः च, तैः
samasa.literal: by those whose senses are well restrained and whose essence (chief concern) is reality
samasa.alt: Also read as a single bahuvrīhi, सुनियतेन्द्रियत्वम् एव तत्त्वसारः येषाम् ‘for whom the restraint of the senses is the heart of the matter’; the first analysis is simpler.
Also upapada: मोक्षम् अर्थयन्ते इति मोक्षार्थिनः.

samasa.vigraha: अस्ताः समस्ताः दोषाः यैः ते, तैः
samasa.literal: by those by whom all faults are thrown off

morph.note: Passive present of अभि + √अस् ‘to throw’ (divādi अस्यति): with अभि it means ‘to practise, repeat, apply oneself to’. The agent is मुनिभिः: the Goddess is the object of the sages’ discipline.
Instrumental plural of the in-stem अर्थिन् ‘one who seeks’ (from अर्थ ‘aim’): -इभिः.
With the correlative सा and the adjectives परमा, भगवती, the predicate picks up 1.57 (सा विद्या परमा मुक्तेर्हेतुभूता सनातनी).

mantras.anvaya: देवि, या त्वं मुक्तिहेतुः अविचिन्त्यमहाव्रता (असि), सुनियतेन्द्रियतत्त्वसारैः अस्तसमस्तदोषैः मोक्षार्थिभिः मुनिभिः अभ्यस्यसे, सा (त्वं) परमा भगवती विद्या असि हि।
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause (या … अभ्यस्यसे) with two predicates and a passive verb whose agent is मुनिभिः and its three epithets; the main clause is सा … विद्या असि.
mantras.lit: You who are the cause of liberation, whose great vow is unthinkable, who are practised by sages seeking liberation, their senses well restrained, holding reality as the essence, all faults cast off — you are that supreme, blessed Knowledge, O Devī.
mantras.tr: You are the cause of liberation, your great discipline beyond thought. Sages who seek release — senses held in check, intent on the truth, every fault cast off — make you their practice. You, O Devī, are that blessed and supreme Knowledge.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Make you their practice’ turns the passive अभ्यस्यसे (‘you are practised’) active.

comm.t: After the ritual words of 4.8 the hymn names the Goddess as the goal of contemplative practice: the knowledge (vidyā) that liberates, pursued by disciplined sages.

The stanza echoes Medhas’s teaching in chapter 1: सा विद्या परमा मुक्तेर्हेतुभूता सनातनी (1.57), and the gods’ hymn in chapter 11 calls her मुक्तिहेतुः again (11.5). The same Goddess who binds as Mahāmāyā (1.55) is the knowledge that releases.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) also names the Goddess विद्या (name 549) and मुक्तिरूपिणी (name 737).

samasa.vigraha: ऋचः च यजूंषि च ऋग्यजूंषि; सुविमलानि ऋग्यजूंषि, तेषाम्

samasa.vigraha: पदानां पाठः पदपाठः; उद्गीथेन रम्यः पदपाठः उद्गीथरम्यपदपाठः; सः एषाम् अस्ति इति उद्गीथरम्यपदपाठवन्ति, तेषाम्

samasa.literal: possessing a recitation of words delightful with the udgītha
samasa.sense: the Sāman chants, sung with the udgītha

samasa.literal: for the causing-to-be of the world
samasa.sense: for the world’s coming into being and welfare
she who ends the worst distress
samasa.alt: परम may also qualify the whole (‘the supreme destroyer of distress’); the karmadhāraya परमा आर्तिः is the natural reading.

morph.note: Genitive plural of the n-stem सामन्: the a of -man is dropped before the ending (साम्नाम्).
हन्तृ is the agent noun of √हन् (kṛt tṛc); its feminine takes ṅīp: हन्त्री ‘she who slays’. In the compound the outside genitive सर्वजगताम् goes with आर्ति: ‘the distress of all worlds’.
Genitive plural of a possessive stem in -वत् (matup): -वताम्. It agrees with साम्नाम्.

mantras.anvaya: (त्वं) शब्दात्मिका सुविमलर्ग्यजुषाम् उद्गीथरम्यपदपाठवतां साम्नां च निधानम् (असि)। भगवती देवी (त्वं) भवभावनाय त्रयी (असि), सर्वजगतां परमार्तिहन्त्री वार्ता च (असि)।
mantras.anvaya_en: Nominal sentences with the verb ‘are’ understood. भवभावनाय is taken with त्रयी (the Veda for the world’s sustenance); it may also go with both त्रयी and वार्ता.
mantras.lit: Having sound as your self, you are the repository of the very pure Ṛk and Yajus and of the Sāmans, which possess a recitation of words delightful with the udgītha. You, the Blessed Devī, are the Triple (Veda) for the bringing-forth of the world, and Vārttā, the destroyer of the supreme distress of all the worlds.
mantras.tr: Your very self is sound: you are the treasure-house of the spotless Ṛk and Yajus and of the Sāman chants, lovely in their words with the udgītha. Blessed Devī, you are the Triple Veda, for the sustaining of the world, and you are Vārttā, the livelihood that ends the deepest distress of all the worlds.
mantras.tr_note: Vārttā, a technical name, is glossed as ‘livelihood’ (agriculture, cattle and trade); ‘sustaining’ interprets भावन ‘causing to be’.

comm.t: The Goddess is the Veda as sound: the Ṛk, the Yajus and the sung Sāman, whose central chant is the udgītha. She is also Vārttā, the knowledge by which people earn their living: the sacred and the practical are both her forms.

Trayī (the threefold Veda) and Vārttā (agriculture, cattle-rearing and trade) are two of the four branches of knowledge in the classical list known from the Arthaśāstra, with ānvīkṣikī (reasoning) and daṇḍanīti (government). Brahmā’s hymn had called her स्वरात्मिका, ‘whose self is the sounded syllable’ (1.73); here she is शब्दात्मिका.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) names the Goddess त्रयी (name 872).
